A.summary:
This commit adds CachingAiProvider, a wrapper around any AiProvider that
stores AI responses in a separate local SQLite database, response_cache.db.
Identical requests are then answered from disk instead of calling the model
again, which saves tokens, cost and time when the same prompts are replayed,
for example when re-reviewing the same patches.

The cache key is a SHA-256 hash of the serialized request, with fields that
vary between runs (context_tag and thought signatures) removed. On a hit,
the stored response is returned immediately. The log records whether the
entry came from this session or a previous one, and how many tokens were
saved. The cached_tokens usage counter is raised by the prompt token count.
On a miss, the request goes to the underlying provider and the response is
stored. Entries older than a TTL are deleted at startup.

A new helper, create_provider_cached(), optionally wraps the configured
provider with this cache. The cache file is placed next to the main
database file.

The diff only adds the wrapper, the helper and the module declaration. It
does not add a settings field or call the helper from anywhere, so the
[ai] response_cache_ttl_days option described in the commit message is not
parsed in this change. Until a caller is wired up, the change has no
user-visible effect, and no Before/After example applies.
A.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::compute_cache_key and
  generate_content), the cache key hashes only the serialized AiRequest,
  which has no model or provider field, and the lookup filters on
  request_hash alone. After changing ai.model, ai.provider, base_url or
  max_tokens, an identical request within the TTL returns the stored
  response from the old configuration, with only an info log line. Mix the
  model name and out-of-request settings into the hash.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/mod.rs (create_provider_cached), database.url is
  treated as a filesystem path with no scheme check. Database::new accepts
  libsql://, https:// and :memory: URLs, so the derived path is bogus (and
  Builder::new_local will likely fail), or for :memory: resolves to a bare
  file in the CWD because the parent is an empty string, not None. Also,
  CachingAiProvider::new logs the derived path without redact_secret, so
  credentials embedded in a URL would reach the INFO log.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/mod.rs (create_provider_cached) and src/settings.rs
  (AiSettings), the cache is unreachable: create_provider_cached has no
  callers, and AiSettings has no response_cache_ttl_days field. The key
  documented in the commit message is silently ignored by serde, so an
  operator who sets it believes caching is configured while every call
  still goes uncached. No Settings.toml, example or docs update is made.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::generate_content), every
  Ok response from the inner provider is stored before any validation,
  including truncated and malformed ones. The full-run restart loop in
  src/bin/review.rs and the reviewer retries rebuild byte-identical early
  stage requests, which then replay the same bad output until the TTL
  expires, defeating retries. Skip the insert when the response is
  truncated, or evict the entry when validation fails.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::generate_content), a
  cache hit sets cached_tokens to the stored cached_tokens plus
  prompt_tokens. The stored usage may already carry a cached count, so the
  result can exceed prompt_tokens, breaking the AiUsage contract. The whole
  prompt was served locally, so the value should be prompt_tokens. Cached
  token figures in ai_interactions and statistics are wrong, and consumers
  using saturating_sub can hide budget accounting.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::generate_content and
  new), cache read errors fail the LLM call. The SELECT path uses await?
  on query, rows.next and row.get, so any libsql error (SQLITE_BUSY past
  the busy timeout, a corrupt file) returns Err before the inner provider
  runs, even though the write path is best-effort. A lookup failure should
  degrade to a miss with a warning. A failed TTL reap is also silently
  ignored, and init errors in new block all LLM use.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::new and
  generate_content), the response cache grows without bound. Expiry runs
  only once at construction, so a long-lived daemon never reaps. Every
  miss stores the full request (system prompt, diff, tool history) in
  request_json, which is never read back, and each tool-loop turn is a
  distinct key. There is no row or byte cap and no index on created_at.
  This violates the bounded disk growth rules in resource-limits.md, and
  untrusted patch content is retained on disk.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider), 171 lines are added with
  no test module. Key canonicalization (context_tag and thought_signature
  stripping), TTL reaping including ttl_days of 0, the hit path skipping
  the inner provider, miss persistence, corrupt-row fallthrough and the
  cached_tokens adjustment are all untested. A key regression would
  silently return wrong cached reviews. Use a mock AiProvider and a
  tempfile::TempDir-backed path.

- [MEDIUM] The commit message describes mechanics (SHA-256 key, TTL,
  logging) but not the problem being solved, whether the cache is meant
  for the daemon or only for local and benchmark use, or the staleness
  hazard of replaying stored LLM output. It also advertises a
  configuration key without saying it is not wired up.

- [LOW] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::generate_content), if a
  stored row fails to deserialize into AiResponse, the code falls through
  to the miss path with the Rows cursor still alive across the inner LLM
  await. The unfinished statement can hold a read snapshot, stalling WAL
  checkpoints, and the later INSERT can fail with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT.
  That error is discarded, so the corrupt row is never replaced. Drop the
  rows before the inner call, or delete the corrupt row.

- [LOW] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::generate_content), the
  INSERT OR REPLACE result is dropped with let _ = and nothing is logged.
  A full disk, SQLITE_BUSY or corruption leaves the cache permanently
  ineffective while it appears enabled, and operators cannot tell. Emit a
  warn! on failure.

- [LOW] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::new), ttl_days as i64 * 86400
  is unchecked. A value of 2^63 or more goes negative after the cast (for
  example u64::MAX gives a cutoff of now plus 86400), so the startup DELETE
  removes every cached row. Larger products overflow, panicking in debug
  builds and wrapping in release. Use i64::try_from with saturating_mul.

- [LOW] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::generate_content), the
  INSERT binds caps.model_name to both the provider and model columns, so
  the provider column duplicates the model name. Anything later reading
  provider from this table gets wrong data.

findings.problem: cache hit inflates cached_tokens beyond prompt_tokens
findings.explanation: On a hit, CachingAiProvider::generate_content sets usage.cached_tokens = stored cached_tokens + prompt_tokens. The stored usage is the original provider usage and may already carry a cached count, so the result can exceed prompt_tokens. That breaks the AiUsage contract that cached_tokens is a breakdown of prompt_tokens. The correct value is prompt_tokens, since the whole prompt was served locally. Consequences: the tokens_cached figures recorded in ai_interactions and cache statistics are wrong. Consumers that compute prompt_tokens.saturating_sub(cached) saturate to zero, which can hide budget accounting. This is a contained accounting defect, and the cache is not wired into any entry point yet.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Adds to the stored cached count instead of setting it to prompt_tokens.

findings.problem: cache read errors fail the LLM call instead of acting as a miss
findings.explanation: In CachingAiProvider::generate_content the SELECT path uses .await? on query, rows.next() and row.get(). Any libsql error (for example SQLITE_BUSY past the 5s busy_timeout when several processes share response_cache.db, or a corrupt file) returns Err before the inner provider is called. The cache is only an optimization, and the write path is deliberately best-effort, so a lookup failure should degrade to a miss with a warning. Immediate consequence: the stage and review fail although the provider was healthy. Downstream, the failed review is retried. CachingAiProvider::new also uses ? throughout, so any cache init error blocks all LLM use. The failed reap and write are also not logged.

locations.why_this_location_matters: A cache read failure propagates as a call failure instead of falling through to the inner provider.
A failed TTL reap is silently ignored.

findings.problem: response cache grows without bound and stores unused request_json
findings.explanation: The expiry DELETE runs only once, in CachingAiProvider::new. A long-lived daemon therefore never reaps while running. generate_content inserts a row on every miss with the full serialized request (system prompt, diff, tool history) in request_json, and the SELECT never reads that column, so it only costs disk. Each tool-loop turn is a distinct key, so rows accumulate roughly quadratically with turns per review. There is no row or byte cap, no index on created_at for the reap scan, and no compaction. Consequences: unbounded response_cache.db and WAL growth until restart, and a slow full-scan reap at startup. Untrusted patch content is also retained on disk. This violates the bounded-disk-growth guidance in patterns/resource-limits.md. Severity is Medium because the cache is not yet wired into any entry point.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Every miss persists the full request and response, with request_json never read back.

findings.problem: cache write failures are silently discarded without logging
findings.explanation: The INSERT OR REPLACE result in CachingAiProvider::generate_content is dropped with let _ =, so a full disk, SQLITE_BUSY or corruption leaves the cache permanently ineffective while it appears enabled. A response_json that fails to deserialize falls through as a miss and the row is only repaired if the later insert succeeds. Best-effort writes are intentional, but no tracing::warn! is emitted. Consequence: operators cannot tell that the cache is not persisting. Low because the review itself is unaffected.

findings.problem: cache INSERT stores model name in the provider column
findings.explanation: The INSERT binds caps.model_name.clone() for provider and caps.model_name for model, so the provider column is a duplicate of the model name. The columns are descriptive only, but anything that later reads provider from this table gets the model name. The consequence is limited to a bookkeeping discrepancy.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The same value is written to both columns.

findings.problem: unchecked ttl_days cast and multiply can wipe the cache
findings.explanation: In CachingAiProvider::new, ttl_days as i64 * 86400 is unchecked. A configured value of 2^63 or more becomes negative after the cast. For example u64::MAX gives -86400, so the cutoff is now + 86400 and the startup DELETE removes every cached row. Larger products can overflow, which panics in debug builds and wraps in release. The value comes from operator configuration, not untrusted input, so impact is limited to losing cache contents. Use i64::try_from with saturating_mul.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Unchecked cast and multiply on a configurable value.

findings.problem: CachingAiProvider added without any tests
findings.explanation: src/ai/cache.rs adds 171 lines with no #[cfg(test)] module. Untested behavior includes key canonicalization (context_tag and thought_signature stripping, distinct content giving distinct keys), TTL reaping including ttl_days = 0, the hit path returning without calling the inner provider, the miss path persisting, a corrupt row falling through, and the cached_tokens adjustment. A regression in the key function would silently return wrong cached reviews. A mock AiProvider and a tempfile::TempDir-backed path would make tests deterministic.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Key logic determines cache correctness and has no test.

findings.problem: cache commit message gives no motivation or intended scope
findings.explanation: The commit adds a non-trivial persistence layer that replays stored LLM output. The message describes mechanics (SHA-256 key, TTL, logging) but not the problem being solved (for example development or benchmark iteration cost), whether it is meant for the daemon or only local and benchmark use, or the staleness hazard. It also advertises a configuration key without saying that it is not wired up. Signed-off-by has a real name, so only the missing why is the defect.

findings.problem: response cache key ignores model and provider settings
findings.explanation: Severity reasoning: the cache is opt-in (create_provider_cached takes enable_cache) and has no caller in src/ at this commit, so blast radius is limited to deployments that turn it on. When it is on, the consequence is silent wrong output: a review is served from a different model or setting with only an info log line, and no error appears anywhere. That is a review-quality and cost-accounting defect, not a crash or data loss, so Medium rather than High. Proof: AiRequest in src/ai/mod.rs has only system, messages, tools, temperature, response_format and context_tag. It has no model or provider field, so the model name and settings such as max_tokens, base_url and thinking reach the provider through its own configuration and are never serialized into the request. compute_cache_key hashes serde_json::to_value(request) minus context_tag and thought signatures, and generate_content looks up by request_hash only. The insert stores caps.model_name in both the provider and model columns, but the SELECT never reads them. A grep for cache_identity over src/ at the target commit and at HEAD returns no matches, and git_log for the range target..HEAD is empty, so no later patch adds a mechanism that mixes model or settings into the key. After changing ai.model, ai.provider, base_url or max_tokens, an identical request within the TTL (default 7 days) returns the stored response from the previous configuration. The defect is not resolved at the series end. The same file can also be shared by binaries configured with different models, because the path is derived from the database directory. A fix would fold the model name and any settings outside the request body into the hash (for example a cache_identity string on AiProvider, which CachingAiProvider hashes together with the request) and add a test that different configurations produce different keys.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The key is derived from the serialized AiRequest alone. AiRequest has no model or provider field, so nothing identifying the model or its settings enters the hash.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The lookup filters on request_hash only. The provider and model columns that are stored on insert are ignored, so a hit from a different model is returned as-is.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The serialized request has no model field, which confirms that the model and provider settings are absent from the hashed material.

findings.problem: create_provider_cached treats database.url as a filesystem path
findings.explanation: Impact is contained to the opt-in response cache, so Medium. It does not corrupt data or send mail. Enabling the cache either fails provider creation or puts the cache file in an unintended place. A credentialed URL is also logged unredacted. I could not confirm the trigger path in this tree: at this commit create_provider_cached has no callers (git_grep finds only its definition at src/ai/mod.rs:182), and I did not check libsql's behaviour when new_local gets a missing directory. The defect is therefore structural, with the reach depending on the later wiring. Verified facts: (1) Database::new in src/db.rs:370-375 explicitly accepts remote URLs, using Builder::new_remote when url starts with libsql:// or https://, and Builder::new_local otherwise. So DatabaseSettings.url (a plain String, src/settings.rs:20) can be remote or :memory:. (2) create_provider_cached runs Path::new(&settings.database.url).parent().unwrap_or(".").join("response_cache.db") with no scheme check. For libsql://host/db the parent is libsql://host, giving the path libsql://host/response_cache.db. That is a relative path with nonexistent directories 'libsql:' and 'host', so Builder::new_local in CachingAiProvider::new will very likely fail, and the ? aborts provider creation. For :memory: the parent is Some(""), not None, so the unwrap_or(".") fallback does not fire. The result is the bare relative path response_cache.db in the process CWD. (3) CachingAiProvider::new logs info!("Response cache enabled ({})", cache_path) with no redact_secret, while Database::new redacts the same URL via crate::utils::redact_secret. If the URL embeds credentials (https://user:pass@host/db), the parent keeps them, so they reach the INFO log and the SQLite path. The token field is separate and is not leaked. (4) Settings::local_token_path, the fallback to '.' for a remote database URL that the candidate mentions, does not exist at this commit (git_grep for local_token_path returns no matches), so no existing helper handles the remote case. The project's own guide describes the intended behaviour as 'a remote URL must never be treated as a path, since its credentials would become a directory name, and a bare filename must not resolve to an empty parent'. This code violates both halves.

locations.why_this_location_matters: A database URL that may be libsql://, https://, or :memory: is parsed as a filesystem path with no scheme check, producing a bogus path or an empty-parent path in the CWD.
The derived path is logged without redact_secret, so a URL with embedded credentials would appear in the INFO log.

findings.problem: response cache is unreachable and its documented TTL key does not exist
findings.explanation: Medium: a contained functional and documentation defect with no data loss, mail, or security impact. The series is a single commit (git_log of 7ff827d^..HEAD returns only this commit), so no later patch wires the feature up. A tree-wide git_grep for create_provider_cached|response_cache|CachingAiProvider at HEAD matches only src/ai/cache.rs and src/ai/mod.rs, and the only mention of create_provider_cached is its definition at src/ai/mod.rs:182. Nothing calls it, so CachingAiProvider can never be constructed at runtime. The enable_cache and cache_ttl_days parameters have no source. src/settings.rs:169 shows AiSettings with only #[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Clone)] and #[allow(unused)], so it has no response_cache or response_cache_ttl_days field and no deny_unknown_fields attribute. The commit message tells operators to write '[ai] response_cache_ttl_days = 14', and serde will silently ignore that key. The operator believes caching is configured, but every call still goes through create_provider with no cache and no 7-day TTL. This is not a startup failure, and no reviews are lost. The feature is dead code that its own commit message advertises as working, and the commit message's documented configuration contradicts the code. Per the settings guide, a new key should be added with a serde default, in Settings.toml, in docs/examples/Settings.example.toml, and in docs/configuration.md; none of that is done here.

findings.problem: response cache stores unvalidated and truncated responses
findings.explanation: Medium: contained retry-defeat that only applies when the opt-in cache is enabled. It affects individual reviews, not the daemon or other data, and it is bounded by the TTL (default 7 days). CachingAiProvider::generate_content (src/ai/cache.rs:130-153) inserts every Ok response from the inner provider into response_cache. This happens before any caller validation, and it includes responses with truncated=true and malformed JSON. The key is a SHA-256 of the serialized AiRequest, and it contains the full message history. Retries that stay inside one run are mostly not affected. The validation retry in src/worker/prompts.rs (inner/outer attempts) appends a 'Previous attempt was rejected' reminder to the prompt, so those requests hash differently and get a fresh sample. Transport errors return via '?' before the insert, so they are not cached. The defect is the full-run restart: src/bin/review.rs loops 'for attempt in 1..=3' with 'Restarting AI review', and reviewer.rs retries up to review.max_retries. A restart rebuilds the same stage prompts, and the key ignores context_tag. Every stage up to and including the failing one is therefore a byte-identical request and is replayed from the cache. The default settings.ai.temperature is 1.0, so a restart would normally re-sample. The cache instead replays the same bad output, the same truncation or the same malformed JSON until the TTL expires. Restarts and re-reviews of the same patch hit the same failure, and the retry loops spend their attempts without any change. Retries are the intended recovery path, and the response is stored without knowing whether it was accepted. I could not read src/ai/session.rs at this revision, and create_provider_cached has no callers in this commit, so the exact wiring is unverified. That is why this is capped at Medium. Replay of valid answers is the intended behavior of the cache. The defect is caching answers that were not accepted, especially truncated ones. A fix is to skip the insert when resp.truncated is set, or to evict the entry when validation fails.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The response is stored without checking truncated or validity, so a bad sample is replayed on any identical request.

locations.code_snippet: INSERT OR REPLACE INTO response_cache (request_hash, provider, model, request_json, response_json, tokens_saved, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
locations.why_this_location_matters: The insert is unconditional on the response contents, so truncated or malformed output is persisted for the TTL.
A full-run restart rebuilds identical early-stage requests, which hit the cached bad responses instead of re-sampling.

findings.problem: cache SELECT cursor stays live across inner provider await on parse failure
findings.explanation: Low: the trigger needs a stored row whose response_json no longer deserializes into AiResponse (for example after a schema change to AiResponse between sessions). The consequence is limited to a stalled WAL checkpoint and a possibly lost cache write, with no effect on review output. In generate_content, `rows` is a `let mut rows` at function scope and is advanced once with `rows.next().await?`. When a row is returned but `serde_json::from_str::<AiResponse>` fails, the code falls through to the miss path and `self.inner.generate_content(request.clone()).await` with the Rows still alive, because Rust drops it only at function exit. The cursor has not been stepped to SQLITE_DONE, so the prepared statement is neither reset nor finalized. In SQLite that keeps a read transaction and its WAL snapshot open on the shared connection. The inner call is an LLM request that can take minutes. During that time (1) WAL checkpoints cannot advance past that snapshot, so the WAL can grow, and (2) the later `INSERT OR REPLACE` runs on the same connection with the read snapshot still open. It can fail with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT if another connection, such as a review worker subprocess or another task, committed in the meantime. That error is discarded by `let _ = self.conn.execute(...)`, so the corrupt row is not replaced and every later call repeats the miss and the full LLM cost. I could not check libsql's exact Rows drop behavior in this repository, so the SQLite-level consequences are from SQLite semantics, not from code I read here. This is therefore capped at Low. The same cursor lifetime also applies when the lookup finds no row, but in that case the statement has already reached DONE and holds no snapshot. The fix is to scope the query in an inner block, or drop(rows) before the inner await. A corrupt row could also be deleted explicitly.

locations.code_snippet: let mut rows = self.conn.query("SELECT response_json, tokens_saved, created_at FROM response_cache WHERE request_hash = ?", libsql::params![hash.clone()]).await?; ... if let Ok(mut resp) = serde_json::from_str::<AiResponse>(&response_json) { ... return Ok(resp); } ... let resp = self.inner.generate_content(request.clone()).await?;
locations.why_this_location_matters: On a parse failure `rows` is not dropped before the inner await, and the later INSERT error is swallowed with `let _ =`.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: compute_cache_key uses unwrap_or_default on serde_json::to_value and serde_json::to_string, so a serialization failure would collapse every request to one constant cache key and replay the first cached response for unrelated requests.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: The failure cannot occur for AiRequest. (1) AiRequest, AiMessage, ToolCall, AiTool, AiResponseFormat and AiRole all use plain #[derive(Serialize)]. A grep for 'impl.*Serialize for|serialize_with|arbitrary_precision|preserve_order' across src/ found only a deserialize_with in src/settings.rs, which is unrelated. So there are no custom Serialize impls that can return Err. (2) Every field is a String, Option<String>, Vec of derived structs, an enum, Option<f32>, or serde_json::Value. There are no maps with non-string keys, no Mutex or RefCell fields, and no unsupported types, which are the usual causes of to_value errors. Value fields (ToolCall.arguments, AiTool.parameters, the schema) are already JSON values, so re-serializing them is infallible. (3) The one value that could be problematic is temperature: Option<f32>. serde_json's Value serializer maps non-finite floats (NaN or infinity) to Value::Null rather than returning Err. The result is a distinct but valid key, not a constant one. (4) serde_json::to_string on a serde_json::Value cannot fail, because all object keys are strings and the Writer is an in-memory Vec. Cargo.toml declares serde_json = "1.0.148" with no features, so arbitrary_precision is not enabled. Since the Err branch is unreachable, unwrap_or_default never fires and a constant-key collision cannot happen. The only theoretical residue is a style preference for propagating the error, not a defect. Cache-key collisions from context_tag or thought signatures being stripped are intentional and out of scope for this candidate.

locations.why_this_location_matters: This is the swallowed-error site, but serializing a serde_json::Value never returns Err.

locations.code_snippet:
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]

B.summary:
This change adds CachingAiProvider, a wrapper around any AiProvider that
stores model responses in a separate local SQLite file, response_cache.db,
and replays them when an identical request is seen again. The goal is to
stop paying for repeated identical model calls, for example when a review
is re-run.

The cache key is a SHA-256 hash of the serialized AiRequest, with the
nondeterministic fields context_tag and thought_signature removed first.
On a hit, the stored response is returned without calling the underlying
provider. A log line records whether the entry came from this session or a
previous one, plus the tokens saved, and usage.cached_tokens is increased
by the prompt token count. On a miss, the inner provider is called and the
response is written to the cache.

Expired entries are deleted at startup, using a TTL from the new config key
response_cache_ttl_days (default 7 days). A new helper,
create_provider_cached(), optionally wraps whatever create_provider()
builds, and places the cache file next to the configured database.

Before:
  Every call to generate_content went straight to the configured
  provider. An identical request sent twice was billed twice, and no
  response_cache.db file existed.

After:
  With caching enabled via create_provider_cached(), the second identical
  request is answered from response_cache.db. The log shows a line like
  "Cache hit [a1b2c3d4e5f6] (previous session) - 5230 tokens saved", and
  the returned usage reports the prompt tokens as cached. Entries older
  than response_cache_ttl_days (for example 14 under [ai]) are removed at
  startup. Deleting response_cache.db clears the cache by hand.
B.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::compute_cache_key and
  generate_content), the cache key hashes only the AiRequest, and the lookup
  filters on request_hash alone. Provider and model identity are never part
  of the key, and the provider and model columns are written but never
  compared on read. After ai.provider or ai.model changes, an identical
  request returns the previous model's stored answer for up to ttl_days (7
  by default), logged as an ordinary cache hit. Benchmark and review output
  is then attributed to a model that never ran.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::generate_content and
  CachingAiProvider::new), cache errors are handled inconsistently. The
  INSERT OR REPLACE result is dropped with let _ =, the WAL and busy_timeout
  PRAGMA results are discarded, and a failed expiry DELETE is ignored, so
  expired rows can be served past the TTL with no log line. "Response cache
  enabled" is logged regardless. An undecodable stored row silently falls
  through to a miss. On the read side, query, rows.next and row.get abort the
  real AI call with ?, so an optional cache can fail a request the provider
  would have served. A cache that never persists looks identical to a
  working one.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/mod.rs (create_provider_cached), the commit message
  claims a working cache and the config key [ai] response_cache_ttl_days,
  but the diff does not contain that behaviour. create_provider_cached has
  no caller. src/reviewer.rs, src/bin/review.rs and src/bin/benchmark.rs
  still call create_provider directly. AiSettings in src/settings.rs has no
  TTL or enable field. A user who sets the documented key gets nothing, and
  the described reaping and hit logging cannot run from any binary.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider), the new persistent cache
  has no test module. Dropping the context_tag removal or
  scrub_thought_signatures, inverting the TTL cutoff comparison, or skipping
  the lookup would leave the suite green. Sibling modules carry tests. The
  cutoff arithmetic in CachingAiProvider::new (ttl_days as i64 * 86400) is
  unchecked, so a very large configured TTL can wrap to a future cutoff and
  delete every row. The commit also does not say what workload motivates
  caching nondeterministic LLM output, which pins one sampled answer per
  request. A fake AiProvider with a call counter and a temp-dir database
  would cover this.

- [MEDIUM] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::generate_content), every
  Ok response is stored without checking for empty content or tool_calls,
  and the key drops only context_tag and thought signatures. Once the cache
  is wired into the reviewer's provider, a retry of the same request after a
  null or degenerate response would replay the bad answer for the whole TTL,
  and the model would never be asked again. As committed this cannot happen,
  because nothing constructs the cache: src/reviewer.rs still uses
  create_provider. Reject empty or truncated responses before the INSERT.

- [LOW] In src/ai/mod.rs (create_provider_cached), the cache path is built
  by treating database.url as a filesystem path. In src/db.rs
  (Database::new), that value can be a libsql:// or https:// URL, which
  yields a nonexistent relative directory (and ':' is illegal on NTFS), so
  the open fails. For ':memory:' the parent is empty, so a persistent
  response_cache.db lands in the process working directory. A later run
  could be answered from stale entries, and under cron or systemd the
  working directory differs from a terminal's.

- [LOW] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::generate_content), a cache
  hit sets cached_tokens to the stored cached_tokens plus the full
  prompt_tokens. The value can exceed prompt_tokens: prompt 1000 with cached
  200 replays as 1200. src/worker/prompts.rs sums it into the interaction
  totals persisted as tokens_cached, and the stats query in src/db.rs
  aggregates it, so tokens_cached can exceed tokens_in. A local replay also
  cannot be told apart from a provider-side prompt-cache hit. The logged
  tokens_saved (prompt plus completion) disagrees with the usage field,
  which credits only the prompt. The review budget in src/reviewer.rs uses
  saturating_sub, so it is not affected.

- [LOW] In src/ai/cache.rs (CachingAiProvider::generate_content), when a
  cached row exists but AiResponse deserialization fails, the rows cursor
  stays open across the whole inner provider call. This can pin a WAL read
  snapshot on response_cache.db and delay checkpoints. The failure is also
  not logged, so schema drift reads as a plain cache miss. The hold lasts
  one provider call, and this relies on standard SQLite semantics because
  the libsql source was not read. Scope the lookup in a block or drop rows
  before calling the inner provider.

findings.problem: replayed hit inflates cached_tokens, can exceed prompt_tokens
findings.type: Misleading usage accounting and plaintext data at rest
findings.explanation: Consequence: persisted and reported token statistics are wrong for any review that gets a local cache hit. No money, secret or live-store write is involved, and the review budget stays safe. Reachability: CachingAiProvider::generate_content runs on every hit, but the wrapper is only built by create_provider_cached(enable_cache=true), and grep finds no caller of that function in src/, so it is opt-in and unwired at this commit. Proof: on a hit, src/ai/cache.rs sets usage.cached_tokens = Some(stored cached_tokens + prompt_tokens) and leaves prompt_tokens, completion_tokens and total_tokens as recorded from the original live call. (1) If the original response already reported cached_tokens (claude, bedrock, gemini and the CLI providers do), the replayed value is original_cached + prompt_tokens, which is greater than prompt_tokens. For example, prompt 1000 with cached 200 replays as cached 1200. (2) Consumers do not subtract it. src/worker/prompts.rs:1201 and :1257 add usage.cached_tokens into t_cached and tokens.2, which become AiInteractionParams.tokens_cached (db.rs:768-780). The stats query at db.rs:1128-1135 then sums tokens_in, tokens_out and tokens_cached per provider, model and status. tokens_cached can therefore exceed tokens_in, and tokens_in and tokens_out count tokens that a replay never spent. (3) A local replay cannot be told apart from a provider-side prompt-cache hit: both land in tokens_cached. The log line's tokens_saved (prompt plus completion) also disagrees with the usage field, which credits only the prompt. What is not affected: src/reviewer.rs:1682 uses prompt_tokens.saturating_sub(cached), so the budget never underflows. On a replay uncached_input is 0 and only completion_tokens are charged, so the budget is overcounted but never exceeded wrongly. quota.rs and token_budget.rs contain no references to cached, total_tokens or prompt_tokens (grep returned nothing), so they are not affected. Unverified: I did not find the readers of the db.rs stats JSON (tokens_cached key), such as a web UI or reports. If one derives cache-hit rate or cost from it, the figure is misleading. Capped at Low for that reason.

findings.problem: cache read cursor stays open across the provider call on bad row
findings.type: Read cursor held across provider call
findings.explanation: Consequence: when a cached row exists but serde_json::from_str::<AiResponse> fails, the cursor stays open during the whole inner LLM call, which can pin a WAL read snapshot on response_cache.db and delay checkpoints. Reachability: CachingAiProvider::generate_content, via create_provider_cached (src/ai/mod.rs:182, the only constructor path found by git_grep). The trigger is a stored response_json that no longer deserializes, for example after AiResponse changes shape between releases, which would affect every old entry. Proof from the code: `let mut rows = self.conn.query(...)` is bound at function scope. `rows.next().await?` returned Some, so the statement was stepped once and not run to DONE. The `if let Ok(..)` fails, control falls through to `self.inner.generate_content(request.clone()).await?`, and `rows` is dropped only at function end. A SQLite statement that has returned a row and not been reset keeps its read transaction, so in WAL mode it holds its snapshot until reset or drop. The checkpointer cannot advance past that snapshot. Blast radius is small: the cache db is a separate single-process file, the later INSERT OR REPLACE runs on the same connection (no self-deadlock), and the hold lasts one provider call. The hit path is not affected because it returns while `rows` is dropped immediately. Assumption not verified: I could not read libsql 0.9.30 (Cargo.lock) source with the available tools, so I am relying on standard SQLite semantics for an un-reset statement, which libsql's local Rows wraps. Reading libsql's Rows/Statement drop and reset behaviour would confirm or refute it. Capped at Low. Fix: scope the lookup in a block, or drop(rows) before the inner call. A related silent path is that a deserialize failure is not logged, so a schema drift reads as 'Cache miss' with no warning.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: compute_cache_key uses unwrap_or_default() on serde_json::to_value and serde_json::to_string, so a serialization failure could give every such request the same constant key.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: Neither call can fail for any AiRequest, so the constant-key path is unreachable. (1) AiRequest (src/ai/mod.rs) contains only: Option<String> system, Vec<AiMessage> messages, Option<Vec<AiTool>> tools, Option<f32> temperature, Option<AiResponseFormat> response_format, and Option<String> context_tag. Every nested type derives Serialize, and none has a hand-written Serialize impl or a non-string-keyed map. The only free-form parts are serde_json::Value fields (ToolCall.arguments, AiTool.parameters, AiResponseFormat::Json.schema), and a Value always has string keys. The usual to_value failure, a map with non-string keys, therefore cannot occur. (2) The non-finite-float case raised in the verification question does not produce an error either. serde_json's Value serializer maps a NaN or infinite f32/f64 to Value::Null instead of failing, because Number cannot hold non-finite values. A NaN temperature thus yields a different key than an absent temperature, which is skipped, so it does not collapse to a constant key. (3) serde_json::to_string on a serde_json::Value is infallible in practice: it has string keys and finite numbers only, so the unwrap_or_default() fallback never runs. (4) The later serde_json::to_string(&request)? in generate_content propagates errors with ?, so even a hypothetical failure would abort before the INSERT. No row could be written under a constant key. No scenario in the current types lets a serialization failure be silently converted into a shared key.
